verses.zh: （大卫的训诲诗，交与伶长。用丝弦的乐器。）　神啊，求你留心听我的祷告，不要隐藏不听我的恳求！
verses.en: For the music director, to be accompanied by stringed instruments; a well-written song[NOTE:1] by David.Listen, O God, to my prayer.Do not ignore[NOTE:2] my appeal for mercy.
notes: Psalm 55. The suffering and oppressed author laments that one of his friends has betrayed him, but he is confident that God will vindicate him by punishing his deceitful enemies.
The meaning of the Hebrew term מַשְׂכִּיל (maskil) is uncertain. See the note on the phrase “well-written song” in the superscription of Ps 52.
verses.commentary:
55:1-3 This, like many Psalms in this section, deals with personal attacks. This
Psalm is particularly painful because the assailants are friends (cf. Ps. 55:12-14).

There are several IMPERATIVES OF REQUEST, one JUSSIVE,
and two COHORTATIVES.

- give ear – BDB 24, KB 27, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, cf. Ps. 5:1; 17:1;
39:12; 49:1; 54:2, etc.

- do not hide Yourself – BDB 761, KB 834, Hithpael IMPERFECT used
in a JUSSIVE sense, cf. Ps. 10:1; Lam. 3:56

- give heed – BDB 904, KB 1151, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, cf. Ps. 5:2;
10:17; 17:1; 61:1; 86:6; 142:6

- answer me – BDB 772, KB 851, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Ps. 4:1; 13:3;
17:6; 38:15; 60:5; 69:13,16,17; 86:1, etc.

- I am restless – BDB 923, KB 1194, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a
COHORTATIVE sense

- rare word used only four times, only here in Wisdom Literature; its meaning is unsure

- JPSOA takes this word as "moan," BDB 242, cf. Ps. 42:12; 43:5; 77:4

- NKJV has "moan (BDB 242) noisily" (BDB 223)

- I am surely distracted (lit. "be noisy") — BDB 223, KB 242, Hiphil
COHORTATIVE, cf. LXX

The reasons for the psalmist's cry for help is given in Ps. 55:3.

- because of the voice of my enemy

- because of the pressure of the wicked (or "voice," see note)

- for they bring down (NET Bible suggests "rain down," cf. Ps. 140:10) upon me

- for in anger they bear a grudge against me

55:2b This line of poetry has two VERBS.

- "restless" ‒ BDB 923, KB 1194, Hiphil IMPERFECT,
cf. Gen. 27:40 (LXX, "vexed," JPSOA, "complaining")

- "distracted" ‒ BDB 223, KB 242, Hiphil COHORTATIVE;
the root has the connotation of an outward show of inner discomfort or agitation. It is
possibly connected to audible sounds, such as murmuring or loud noise, cf. 1 Sam. 4:5;
1 Kgs. 1:45; Ruth 1:19 (LXX, "troubled," JPSOA, "moaning")

55:3b

NASB
"pressure"

NKJV, TEV. JPSOA, Peshitta
"oppression"

REB
"shrill clamour"

NJB
"outcry"

NRSV
"clamor"

LXX
"affliction"

This is a rare root that is understood to mean

- pressure ‒ BDB 734, KB 785

- voice, noise ‒ BDB 873; notice "says" appears in line 3a

verses.zh: 求你侧耳听我，应允我。我哀叹不安，发声唉哼，
verses.en: Pay attention to me and answer me.I am so upset[NOTE:1] and distressed,[NOTE:2] I am beside myself,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “hide yourself from.”
Or “restless” (see Gen 27:40). The Hiphil is intransitive-exhibitive, indicating the outward display of an inner attitude.
Heb “in my complaint.”

verses.zh: 都因仇敌的声音，恶人的欺压；因为他们将罪孽加在我身上，发怒气逼迫我。
verses.en: because of what the enemy says,[NOTE:1] and because of how the wicked[NOTE:2] pressure me,[NOTE:3] for they hurl trouble[NOTE:4] down upon me[NOTE:5] and angrily attack me.
notes: The verb is a Hiphil cohortative from הוּם (hum), which means “to confuse someone” in the Qal and “to go wild” in the Niphal. An Arabic cognate means “to be out of one’s senses, to wander about.” With the vav (ו) conjunctive prefixed to it, the cohortative probably indicates the result or effect of the preceding main verb. Some prefer to emend the form to וְאֵהוֹמָה (veʾehomah), a Niphal of הוּם (hum), or to וְאֶהַמֶה (veʾehameh), a Qal imperfect from הָמָה (hamah, “to moan”). Many also prefer to take this verb with what follows (see v. 3).
Heb “because of [the] voice of [the] enemy.”
The singular forms “enemy” and “wicked” are collective or representative, as the plural verb forms in the second half of the verse indicate.
Heb “from before the pressure of the wicked.” Some suggest the meaning “screech” (note the parallel “voice”; cf. NEB “shrill clamour”; NRSV “clamor”) for the rare noun עָקָה (ʿaqah, “pressure”).
Heb “wickedness,” but here the term refers to the destructive effects of their wicked acts.

verses.zh: 我心在我里面甚是疼痛；死的惊惶临到我身。
verses.en: My heart beats violently[NOTE:1] within me;the horrors of death overcome me.[NOTE:2]
notes: The verb form in the MT appears to be a Hiphil imperfect from the root מוֹט (mot, “to sway”), but the Hiphil occurs only here and in the Kethib (consonantal text) of Ps 140:10, where the form יַמְטֵר (yamter, “let him rain down”) should probably be read. Here in Ps 55:3 it is preferable to read יַמְטִירוּ (yamtiru, “they rain down”). It is odd for “rain down” to be used with an abstract object like “wickedness,” but in Job 20:23 God “rains down” anger (unless one emends the text there; see BHS).
Heb “shakes, trembles.”
verses.commentary:
55:4-8 This strophe describes how the psalmist feels (hyperbolic language) about the attacks
of his adversaries.

- my heart is in anguish within me – BDB 296, KB 297, Qal IMPERFECT, from
root for pain in childbirth

- the terrors of death have fallen upon me – BDB 956, KB 709, Qal PERFECT,
cf. Ps. 18:4-5; 116:3

- fear and trembling come upon me – BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERFECT

- horror has overwhelmed me – BDB 491, KB 487, Piel IMPERFECT
with waw, cf. Isa. 21:4; Ezek. 7:18

In light of these fears he tells what he would like to do to escape them (figurative
language).

- O that I had (lit. "give") wings like a dove – BDB 678, KB 733, Qal
IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense

- I would fly away – BDB 733, KB 800, Qal COHORTATIVE

- I would be at rest – BDB 1014, KB 1496, Qal COHORTATIVE

- I would wander far away – BDB 934, KB 1221, Hiphil IMPERFECT used
in a COHORTATIVE sense

- I would lodge in the wilderness – BDB 533, KB 529, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a COHORTATIVE sense

- I would hasten to my place of refuge – BDB 301, KB 300, Hiphil
COHORTATIVE

- raging wind – BDB 703 (only here)

- tempest – BDB 704

55:4 "heart" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEART.

▣ "the terrors of death" Death is fearful to fallen mankind (cf. Ps. 18:4-5;
116:3), but God is in control of death and will bring it to an end (cf. Isa. 25:8; Hosea 13:14;
1 Cor. 15:50-57; 2 Tim. 1:10).

verses.zh: 恐惧战兢归到我身；惊恐漫过了我。
verses.en: Fear and panic overpower me;[NOTE:1] terror overwhelms[NOTE:2] me.
notes: Heb “the terrors of death have fallen on me.”
Heb “fear and trembling enter into me.”

verses.zh: 我说：但愿我有翅膀像鸽子，我就飞去，得享安息。
verses.en: I say,[NOTE:1] “I wish I had wings like a dove.I would fly away and settle in a safe place.
notes: Heb “covers.” The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) consecutive carries on the descriptive (present progressive) force of the preceding imperfect.

verses.zh: 我必远游，宿在旷野。（细拉）
verses.en: Look, I will escape to a distant place;I will stay in the wilderness. (Selah)
verses.commentary: 55:7 "Selah" See note at Psalm 3:2 and Intro. to Psalms, VII. B. #1.

verses.zh: 我必速速逃到避所，脱离狂风暴雨。
verses.en: I will hurry off to a place that is safefrom the strong wind[NOTE:1] and the gale.”
notes: The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) consecutive carries on the descriptive (present progressive) force of the verbs in v. 5.
verses.commentary:
55:8 "place of refuge" The NOUN ("shelter," BDB 812, KB 618) occurs
only here and Psalm 18:2. The VERBAL form, "deliverer," appears in 2 Sam. 22:2; Ps. 144:2.

verses.zh: 主啊，求你吞灭他们，变乱他们的舌头！因为我在城中见了强暴争竞的事。
verses.en: Confuse them,[NOTE:1] O Lord.Frustrate their plans.[NOTE:2] For I see violence and conflict in the city.
notes: Heb “[the] wind [that] sweeps away.” The verb סָעָה (saʿah, “sweep away”) occurs only here in the OT (see H. R. Cohen, Biblical Hapax Legomena [SBLDS], 120).

Traditionally בַּלַּע (balaʿ) has been taken to mean “swallow” in the sense of “devour” or “destroy” (cf. KJV), but this may be a homonym meaning “confuse” (see BDB 118 s.v. בַּלַּע; HALOT 135 s.v. III *בֶּלַע). “Their tongue” is the understood object of the verb (see the next line).
verses.commentary:
55:9-11 This strophe continues the prayer request of Ps. 55:1-2.

- confuse (lit. "swallow up," i.e., "destroy) – BDB 118, KB 134, Piel
IMPERATIVE; this root could be used in the sense of "confuse,"
cf. Ps. 107:27; Isa. 3:12; 9:16; 19:3; 28:7

- divide their tongues – BDB 811, KB 928, Piel IMPERATIVE; this
may be an allusion to Genesis 11:1-9.

Both #1 and #2 are prayers to disrupt/thwart the plans and schemes of the psalmist's
enemies. Apparently they were causing trouble within the hometown of the psalmist (if David, then
Jerusalem). They are political enemies!

- I have seen violence in the city

- I have seen strife in the city

- day and night they go around her upon her walls

- iniquity is in her midst

- mischief is in her midst

- oppression does not depart her streets (lit. plaza, BDB 932)

- deceit does not depart her streets (lit. plaza/market place)

Numbers 3; 4; 5 may be an allusion to watchmen on the walls. In this case the watchmen
are personified as iniquity and mischief!

55:9

NASB, NKJV, Vulgate
"divide their tongues"

REB
"divide their counsels"

NRSV
"confound their speech"

LXX, TEV
"confuse the speech"

Peshitta
"render useless their tongues"

The MT has "divide" (BDB 811, KB 928, Piel IMPERATIVE). This
is parallel to the first VERB "shallow" (BDB 118, KB 134, Piel IMPERATIVE)
in the sense of "destroy."

The Piel form of "divide" was used of a plowed furrow in farming and came to mean
"divide." It is used here in the sense of spread disunity and divide the enemies of the psalmist, thereby destroying
their hateful, violent, evil words.

verses.zh: 他们在城墙上昼夜绕行；在城内也有罪孽和奸恶。
verses.en: Day and night they walk around on its walls,[NOTE:1] while wickedness and destruction[NOTE:2] are within it.
notes: Heb “split their tongue,” which apparently means “confuse their speech,” or, more paraphrastically, “frustrate the plans they devise with their tongues.”
Heb “day and night they surround it, upon its walls.” Personified “violence and conflict” are the likely subjects. They are compared to watchmen on the city’s walls.

verses.zh: 邪恶在其中；欺压和诡诈不离街市。
verses.en: Disaster is within it;violence[NOTE:1] and deceit do not depart from its public square.
notes: Wickedness and destruction. These terms are also closely associated in Ps 7:14.

verses.zh: 原来不是仇敌辱骂我，若是仇敌，还可忍耐；也不是恨我的人向我狂大，若是恨我的人就必躲避他。
verses.en: Indeed,[NOTE:1] it is not an enemy who insults me,or else I could bear it;it is not one who hates me who arrogantly taunts me,[NOTE:2] or else I could hide from him.
notes: Or “injury, harm.”
Or “for.”
verses.commentary:
55:12-15 This strophe identified those causing the trouble as the psalmist's acquaintances.

- It is not an enemy who reproaches me – I could bear it.

- It is not one who hates me – I could hide from him.

- It is not one who exalted himself against me (cf. Ps. 35:26;
38:16; Job 19:5) – I could hide from him.

- It is you, a man

- my equal (BDB 789, KB 885)

- my companion (BDB 48 I, KB 54 I)

- my familiar friend (BDB 393, KB 390, Pual PARTICIPLE

- We had sweet fellowship together.

- We walked in the house of God together (i.e., worshiped together).

The psalmist reacts to their treachery.

- Let death come deceitfully upon them – Qere, BDB 674, KB 728, Hiphil
IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense (the Hebrew text is
uncertain and emendations are usually made)

- Let them go down to Sheol – BDB 432, KB 434, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense; for Sheol see

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?, I. B.

- The reason for the psalmist's desire for their judgment:

- evil in their dwelling place (BDB 158)

- evil is in their midst

Since #3 does not parallel #2 well, there has been suggestion for
emendation to "habitation."

- "go in terror to their graves"

- "go in terror to the pit" (i.e., "storehouse" in the ground)

verses.zh: 不料是你；你原与我平等，是我的同伴，是我知己的朋友！
verses.en: But it is you,[NOTE:1] a man like me,[NOTE:2] my close friend in whom I confided.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “[who] magnifies against me.” See Pss 35:26; 38:16.
It is you. The psalmist addresses the apparent ringleader of the opposition, an individual who was once his friend.
Heb “a man according to my value,” i.e., “a person such as I.”

verses.zh: 我们素常彼此谈论，以为甘甜；我们与群众在　神的殿中同行。
verses.en: We would share personal thoughts with each other;[NOTE:1] in God’s temple we would walk together among the crowd.
notes: Heb “my close friend, one known by me.”
verses.commentary:
55:14

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, REB
"the throng"

NJB
"then they recoil in disorder"

The Hebrew NOUN (BDB 921, KB 1189) is rare, used only three times in the OT.

- the nations are in an uproar, cf. Ps. 2:1

- a noisy, festival crowd in the temple, cf. Ps. 55:14

- the tumult of those who do iniquity, cf. Ps. 64:2

The VERB form means "be in tumult" or "unrest." But here, it denotes the large
crowd in the temple (or tabernacle) on a regular feast day. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL

verses.zh: 愿死亡忽然临到他们！愿他们活活地下入阴间！因为他们的住处，他们的心中，都是邪恶。
verses.en: May death destroy them.[NOTE:1] May they go down alive into Sheol.[NOTE:2] For evil is in their dwelling place and in their midst.
notes: Heb “who together we would make counsel sweet.” The imperfect verbal forms here and in the next line draw attention to the ongoing nature of the actions (the so-called customary use of the imperfect). Their relationship was characterized by such intimacy and friendship. See IBHS 502-3 §31.2b.

The meaning of the MT is unclear. The Kethib (consonantal text) reads יַשִּׁימָוֶת עָלֵימוֹ (yashimavet ʿalemo, “May devastation [be] upon them.”). The proposed noun יַשִּׁימָוֶת occurs only here and perhaps in the place name Beth Jeshimoth in Num 33:49. The Qere (marginal text) has יַשִּׁי מָוֶת עָלֵימוֹ (yashi mavet ʿalemo). The verbal form יַשִּׁי is apparently an alternate form of יַשִּׁיא (yashiʾ), a Hiphil imperfect from נָשַׁא (nashaʾ, “deceive”). In this case one might read “death will come deceptively upon them.” This reading has the advantage of reading מָוֶת (mavet, “death”) which forms a natural parallel with “Sheol” in the next line. The present translation is based on the following reconstruction of the text: יְשִׁמֵּם מָוֶת (yeshimmem mavet). The verb assumed in the reconstruction is a Hiphil jussive third masculine singular from שָׁמַם (shamam, “be desolate”) with a third masculine plural pronominal suffix attached. This reconstruction assumes that (1) haplography has occurred in the traditional text (the original sequence of three mems [מ] was lost with only one mem remaining), resulting in the fusion of originally distinct forms in the Kethib, and (2) that עָלֵימוֹ (ʿalemo, “upon them”) is a later scribal addition attempting to make sense of a garbled text. The preposition עַל (ʿal) does occur with the verb שָׁמַם (shamam), but in such cases the expression means “be appalled at/because of” (see Jer 49:20; 50:45). If one were to retain the prepositional phrase here, one would have to read the text as follows: יַשִּׁים מָוֶת עָלֵימוֹ (yashim mavet ʿalemo, “Death will be appalled at them”). The idea seems odd, to say the least. Death is not collocated with this verb elsewhere.
verses.commentary:
55:15 "Sheol" Sheol is sometimes depicted as an animal with a wide mouth that swallows
people alive. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD? I. A.

▣

NASB
"For evil is in their dwelling, in their midst"

NKJV
"For wickedness is in their dwellings and among them"

NRSV, TEV
"For evil is in their homes and in their hearts"

NJB
"since evil shares their home with them"

REB
"their homes are haunts of evil!"

JPSOA
"For where they dwell, there is evil"

Peshitta
"because there is evil among them"

LXX
"because evils are in their sojournings, in their midst"

These are parallel lines. I like the NRSV translation, but it is just speculation
on a vague Hebrew poetic line.

verses.zh: 至于我，我要求告　神；耶和华必拯救我。
verses.en: As for me, I will call out to God,and the Lord will deliver me.
verses.commentary:
55:16-21 This strophe describes what God will do for/against

- the psalmist

- his betrayers

Psalm 55:19 is both a description of God (i.e., line 2, "who sits enthroned from of
old," cf. Deut. 33:27; Ps. 45:6; 90:2; 93:2; Lam. 5:19) and the adversaries (i.e., line 3, who do not change). The
confusion arises because line 3 could apply to God (cf. Matt. 3:6, i.e., Malachi 3:6), but here
it refers to the unchanging evil hearts of the psalmist's enemies.

Psalm 55:16-19a gives the psalmist's prayers and God's response.

- I shall call upon God – BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal IMPERFECT used in
a COHORTATIVE sense

- YHWH will save me – BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil IMPERFECT

- I will complain – BDB 967, KB 1319, Qal COHORTATIVE,
cf. Ps. 64:1; 142:2; this root can mean "meditate," cf. Ps. 119:15,23,27,148

- I will murmur – BDB 242, KB 250, Qal IMPERFECT used
in a COHORTATIVE sense

- He will hear my voice – BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERFECT with
waw

- He will redeem my soul from the battle – BDB 804, KB 911, Qal PERFECT, see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

- God will hear, Ps. 55:19a – BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERFECT

In Ps. 55:19a God will answer the adversaries (in the sense of, "give them what
they deserve" — BDB 772, KB 851, Qal IMPERFECT; this root can
mean "answer" or "afflict." We reap what we sow!

Psalm 55:19c-21 describes
their hearts and actions (collective "he," cf. Ps. 55:18b).

- there is no change (no VERB)

- they do not fear God

- they put forth their hands against those who were at peace

- they violated the covenant

- they have smooth speech but have war in their hearts

- their soft words are like drawn swords

All the VERBS in #2-6 are PERFECTS, denoting a settled
attitude of hate and rebellion.

verses.zh: 我要晚上、早晨、晌午哀声悲叹；他也必听我的声音。
verses.en: During the evening, morning, and noontimeI will lament and moan,[NOTE:1] and he will hear[NOTE:2] me.[NOTE:3]
notes: Go down alive. This curse imagines a swift and sudden death for the psalmist’s enemies.
The first verb is clearly a cohortative form, expressing the psalmist’s resolve. The second verb, while formally ambiguous, should also be understood as cohortative here.

The prefixed verb with vav (ו) consecutive normally appears in narrational contexts to indicate past action, but here it continues the anticipatory (future) perspective of the preceding line. In Ps 77:6 one finds the same sequence of cohortative + prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) consecutive. In this case as well, both forms refer to future actions.
verses.commentary:
55:17 "Evening and morning and at noon" The day begins at evening for ancient
Israelites because of Gen. 1:5,8,13,19,23,31. The "at noon" implies a later time when
Judaism had three prayer times (cf. Dan. 6:10):

- at the time of the morning sacrifice (about 9 A.M.)

- noon

- at the time of the evening sacrifice (about 3 P.M.)

It is surely possible that the phrase is an idiom for "continually."

▣ "redeem" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

▣ "soul" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

▣ "in peace" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (OT)

verses.zh: 他救赎我命脱离攻击我的人，使我得享平安，因为与我相争的人甚多。
verses.en: He will rescue[NOTE:1] me and protect me from those who attack me,[NOTE:2] even though[NOTE:3] they greatly outnumber me.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “my voice.”
The perfect verbal form is here used rhetorically to indicate that the action is certain to take place (the so-called perfect of certitude).
Heb “he will redeem in peace my life from [those who] draw near to me.”
Or “for.”

verses.zh: 那没有更变、不敬畏　神的人，从太古常存的　神必听见而苦待他。
verses.en: God, the one who has reigned as king from long ago,will hear and humiliate them.[NOTE:1] (Selah)They refuse to change,and do not fear God.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “among many they are against me.” For other examples of the preposition עִמָּד (ʿimmad) used in the sense of “at, against,” see HALOT 842 s.v.; BDB 767 s.v.; IBHS 219 §11.2.14b.

Heb “God will hear and answer them, even [the] one who sits [from] ancient times.” The prefixed verbal from with vav (ו) consecutive carries on the anticipatory force of the preceding imperfect. The verb appears to be a Qal form from עָנָה (ʿanah, “to answer”). If this reading is retained, the point would be that God “answered” them in judgment. The translation assumes an emendation to the Piel וַיְעַנֵּם (vayeʿannem; see 2 Kgs 17:20) and understands the root as עָנָה (ʿanah, “to afflict”; see also 1 Kgs 8:35).
verses.commentary: 55:19 "Selah" See note at Psalm 3:2 and Intro. to Psalms, VII. B. #1

verses.zh: 他背了约，伸手攻击与他和好的人。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] attacks[NOTE:2] his friends;[NOTE:3] he breaks his solemn promises to them.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “[the ones] for whom there are no changes, and they do not fear God.”
He. This must refer to the psalmist’s former friend, who was addressed previously in vv. 12-14.
Heb “stretches out his hand against.”

The form should probably be emended to an active participle (שֹׁלְמָיו, sholemayv) from the verbal root שָׁלַם (shalam, “be in a covenant of peace with”). Perhaps the translation “his friends” suggests too intimate a relationship. Another option is to translate, “he attacks those who made agreements with him.”

verses.zh: 他的口如奶油光滑，他的心却怀着争战；他的话比油柔和，其实是拔出来的刀。
verses.en: His words are as smooth as butter,[NOTE:1] but he harbors animosity in his heart.[NOTE:2] His words seem softer than oil,but they are really like sharp swords.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he violates his covenant.”

Heb “the butter-like [words] of his mouth are smooth.” The noun מַחְמָאֹת (makhmaʾot, “butter-like [words]”) occurs only here. Many prefer to emend the form to מֵחֶמְאָה (mekhemʾah, from [i.e., “than”] butter”), cf. NEB, NRSV “smoother than butter.” However, in this case “his mouth” does not agree in number with the plural verb חָלְקוּ (khalequ, “they are smooth”). Therefore some further propose an emendation of פִּיו (piv, “his mouth”) to פָּנָיו (panayv, “his face”). In any case, the point seems to that the psalmist’s former friend spoke kindly to him and gave the outward indications of friendship.
Heb “and war [is in] his heart.”
verses.commentary: 55:21 "smoother than butter" This Hebrew form is found only here (BDB 563, same thought in Prov. 5:3).

verses.zh: 你要把你的重担卸给耶和华，他必抚养你；他永不叫义人动摇。
verses.en: Throw your burden[NOTE:1] upon the Lord,and he will sustain you.[NOTE:2] He will never allow the godly to be shaken.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “his words are softer than oil, but they are drawn swords.”
The Hebrew noun occurs only here.
The pronoun is singular; the psalmist addresses each member of his audience individually.
verses.commentary:
55:22-23 This final strophe is a contrast of what God will do for the faithful follower
and against the faithless friend(s).

- the faithful follower

- the psalmist admonishes them to cast (BDB 1020, KB 1527, Hiphil
IMPERATIVE) their burden (i.e., "lot," BDB 396, KB 393, only
here and Ps. 37:5) upon YHWH (cf. 1 Pet. 5:7)

- follow the psalmist's example, "I will trust in You" (v. 23c)

- the faithless friend(s)

- bring them down to the pit of destruction (i.e. death, Sheol)

- men of bloodshed and deceit will live only half their allotted days

In light of the trust of the faithful, YHWH will

- sustain them – BDB 465, KB 463, Pilpel IMPERFECT, cf. Ruth 4:15;
Neh. 9:21

- never allow them to be shaken – BDB 557, cf. Ps. 125:1; Prov. 10:30

Remember, this Psalm describes the pain of betrayal and the many nights of prayer
and discouragement at the actions of faithless friend(s). These last verses are not a promise
of lack of problems but of YHWH's presence and care. In the end all will be set straight. We
live in a fallen world, unfair and ungodly world. Believers suffer and are treated badly but
there is more to life than the immediate circumstances!

One last comment, it is not certain who is speaking in this strophe and, therefore,
to whom they are speaking.

- a priest or prophet hears the psalmist and responds to him

- the psalmist is speaking to

- himself

- his readers

- others hurt by friends

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Who are the enemies? Why are their actions so painful to the psalmist?

- Describe the psalmist's feelings. (cf. Ps. 55:4-8)

- How do Ps. 55:9-11 fit into this Psalm? What city is it referring to?

- What is the problem in interpreting Ps. 55:19?

- Put in your own words the kind of person Ps. 55:21 is talking about.

- Who is speaking Ps. 55:22-23 and to whom?

- List God's actions in Ps. 55:22-23.

verses.zh: 神啊，你必使恶人下入灭亡的坑；流人血、行诡诈的人必活不到半世，但我要倚靠你。
verses.en: But you, O God, will bring them[NOTE:1] down to the deep Pit.[NOTE:2] Violent and deceitful people[NOTE:3] will not live even half a normal life-span.[NOTE:4] But as for me, I trust in you.
notes: Heb “he will never allow swaying for the righteous.”
The pronominal suffix refers to the psalmist’s enemies (see v. 19).
Heb “well of the pit.” The Hebrew term שַׁחַת (shakhat, “pit”) is often used as a title for Sheol (see Pss 16:10; 30:9; 49:9; 103:4).
Heb “men of bloodshed and deceit.”
